Measuring inequality

Placeholder paragraph for the test fixture. The Lorenz curve plots the cumulative percentage of households, from the poorest, against the cumulative percentage of income they hold. If every household had the same income the curve would be the diagonal, the line of equality. Real curves bow below it, and the further they bow the more unequal the distribution. A progressive tax takes a larger share of a larger income, and transfer payments add to the incomes at the bottom, so both move the curve toward the line of equality. The Gini coefficient compares the area between the two curves with the whole area under the diagonal.
